item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Why Re-Signing Evan Phillips is a Must For the Dodgers This Offseason
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers saw eight players enter free agency this offseason, and Evan Phillips is one of a few players who could still have a big role for the Dodgers next year. Phillips isn’t the most important player for the team to retain, as Tarik Skubal and Alex Vesia were both incredibly important to the team last year, but he played a key role in the bullpen during 2026. Why Should the Dodgers Keep Evan Phillips? Phillips struggled upon his return for the Dodgers following Tommy John surge
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers saw eight players enter free agency this offseason, and Evan Phillips is one of a few players who could still have a big role for the Dodgers next year.
Phillips isn’t the most important player for the team to retain, as Tarik Skubal and Alex Vesia were both incredibly important to the team last year, but he played a key role in the bullpen during 2026.
Why Should the Dodgers Keep Evan Phillips?
Phillips struggled upon his return for the Dodgers following Tommy John surgery, posting a 6.14 ERA through his eight games in July—his first month back.
After that, though, he had a couple of really impressive months to close the regular season. He posted a 2.61 ERA in August through 14 appearances, and had a 2.16 ERA through nine appearances in September.
On the year, Phillips had a 3.46 ERA through 26 innings, striking out 33 batters.
His fastball looked good throughout the season, averaging a career-best 96.8 mph during the season. His other pitches played well too, as is evident by his 31.1% strikeout rate and 35.4% chase rate.
Despite his strong chase numbers, though, Phillips was prone to giving up hard-hit fly balls and line drives, grading poorly with an average exit velocity of 91 mph and just a 31.8% ground ball rate. He allowed five home runs on the year, and definitely has to improve in that area if he’s to cut it for the Dodgers.
That being said, the Dodgers also lost Blake Treinen to free agency after the close of the season, and losing another right-handed veteran like Phillips would be a huge blow to their bullpen.
Phillips has historically performed well for the Dodgers over his six years with the team, posting a 2.36 ERA over the course of 232 games with Los Angeles. He is acclimated to high-leverage situations, having served as the Dodgers’ closer in 2023 and 2024, and would be a huge asset for the team.
Do the Dodgers Need Another Right-Handed Reliever?
As it stands, the Dodgers have several right-handers in their ranks, with Edwin Diaz, Edgardo Henriquez and Brock Stewart all commanding spots on the roster as well as Will Klein, Ben Casparius and Jake Cousins all recovering from injuries.
Even with their abundance of left-handers, the Dodgers would do well to keep Phillips as a middle-inning relief pitcher while Diaz, Henriquez and Tanner Scott handle late-inning duties.
While Phillips certainly wasn’t at his best last season, his track record and encouraging performances towards the end of the season warrant a spot on the team, especially for the price he commands.
Would you want the Dodgers to re-sign Evan Phillips?
